title: Annotatio IV §.II: Second fountain — Error of intellect when will-pravity is loosed; near sources of error
pass_a_gloss: The Posterior Fountain is Error of Intellect, which whoever loosens the reins to the will’s pravity is prone to incur — just as, conversely, one who detests malice draws nearer to the truth (Ps. 25:14; Matt. 5:8; John 7:17). But error is born proximately from prejudices, the predominance of affections, also perverse education and information, reading of calumnious books, and the like;
pass_b_english: The second fountain is error of intellect — which anyone who loosens the reins to will-pravity is apt to fall into; conversely, whoever hates malice draws nearer the truth (Ps. 25:14; Matt. 5:8; John 7:17).
Error is born nearby from prejudices, passions in the saddle, warped schooling and teaching, the reading of slanderous books, and the like.
source_text: Posterior Fons, Error Intellectus est, quem pronus incurrit, quisquis voluntatis pravitati habenas laxat, sicuti vice versa, malitiam detestatus, veritati propior imminet. PS. 25. v. 14. Matt. 5. v. 8. Joh. 7. v. 17. Subnascitur autem error proximè ex praejudiciis, affectuum praedominio etiam educatione & informatione perversis, lectione librorum calumniosorum, hisque similibus;
notes: Error Intellectus; Ps 25:14; Matt 5:8; John 7:17; proximate causes.
